title: Truly Unplayable
body: The gameplay was bad to begin with, but is much worse than it should be because of numerous promised QOL updates not being implemented and a severe lack of resources. With the current scenario, you will lose many races due to RNG/AI and need to consume clocks to retry them. But clocks are a rare material compared to how many you need. You can buy 3 a day for coins and cannot buy any more, yet you'll need to use those 3 clocks for a single run. Shockingly, you can't even spend real money to get clocks. You'll go through an hour long run just to get a useless "legacy" 9 times out of 10 because of RNG, and you can only do a certain number of runs per day due to borrow limits. This is extremely frustrating and fatiguing. There are other issues as well. The God-awful localization makes it very difficult to play Uma just for the story (and so does the unforgiving character gacha). There was a big controversy originating from the Discord server recently that showed that Cygames does not care at all about the official server or the fandom. It started with someone sharing Uma x Trainer fanart, which their mods said was against the rules (it wasn't). These mods incited harassment and doxxing against an innocent artist, banned thousands of people, made slanderous comments towards the real-life horses, and promised guidelines from Cygames themselves but never shared any, instead staying silent until the issue "blowed over". So far, Cygames has ignored nearly every issue or request raised by their players. I pushed through these issues and kept playing, but I have truly reached my limit and quit the game a couple weeks ago, as did my friends and clubmates. Even when a new scenario comes out, you can count on Cygames to make it painful to play. Their poor management is really showing in their rapidly declining monthly revenue. Such a shame to see a game with a lot of potential kill itself like this, because I love the characters and enjoyed the Japanese version.

Supports card are basically items that boost your characters and you can hold 5. For them to be effective you need to pull 3-4 copies. If you choose to not summon on supports your characters will be weak, but the banners have just as bad of rates as the actual umamusume, so you’re forced to pick between summoning for characters or a png that makes you stronger. This game genuinely gets ruined by the support card system and it’s a shame because I want to like it, but because of that system it’s just not fun.

title: Doesn’t respect your time, wouldn’t respect your money
body: I’ve been playing it since it released a little over a year ago, and I had a lot of fun with the gameplay! Unfortunately, as time has gone on and they’ve added new career scenarios and different types of events, it’s really started to become a drag. Selecting the “shorten all events” skip option feels like it does next to nothing, and with the number of random events the Trackblazer scenario has, each career takes about maybe 40 minutes if I’m moving as quickly as I can. Most of that time isn’t spent strategizing on what to do, it’s spent waiting for each event and cutscene to give me a choice (if it has one) or end. It might be more tolerable if you could spend double the tp (or whatever the player’s stamina/energy is called) to have it roll 2 umas at the end of the career instead of one, but as it is now I feel like I’m wasting my time to, for the vast majority of the time, get basically nothing. All of that is compounded by the support card system and the way the gacha functions. As far as I know, there is no pity system that guarantees you get an ssr after a certain number of pulls - the only thing you can do is spark them after 200. That might be more passable if it weren’t for the fact that many support cards only unlock the bonuses that make them at best good and at worst usable when you uncap them multiple times, which requires either multiple copies of the card or the use of an item that you can get 1 of maybe every 6-10 months, which is atrocious given the number of support cards in the game and the fact that, because it’s live service, there’s no guarantee the card you uncap now will be viable down the line. All of which is to say, unless you get extremely lucky, the only way to guarantee yourself the support card you want at a level that makes using it feel like it’s actually worth it, you have to spend money (unless you feel like skipping a bunch of banners and even then you’d probably still have to get lucky since every spark takes 30,000 carats). If you enjoy the characters from this game and the Umamusume franchise as a whole, and want to support it monetarily, I would recommend you spend your money elsewhere. Get something that you can keep even if this game eventually comes to the end of its service - a poster, a figure, a plushie, whatever. To me, that’d be worth more than anything this game can currently (and may ever) provide.

title: Mixed but Good
body: Art: 10/10 - the 3d models are done very well; fluid but still anime-like, and there’s even details like wet cloth when it rains. Very good Voice Acting: 7/10 - it’s all done well, but only stories and lobby interactions are fully voiced; career mode is partially voiced. I understand why, but it still feels like a little bit of a letdown Gameplay: 7/10 - actually more interesting than I expected, and strategy is actually really deep Music: 8/10 - everything is quite good but it doesn’t have legendary songs like Idolm@ster or Love Live imo, or legendary soundtrack like Hiroyuki Sawano Characters: 9/10 - I think Tokai Teio is one of the best anime characters of all time and Gold Ship is a hilarious memester. Daiwa Scarlet should just be a generic ambitious tsundere but is somehow much more interesting. Solid in this department. — I really enjoyed my first full career; watching the races and listening to the commentators actually made the emotional stakes pretty high, in a way I was not expecting from a gacha game. The problem with this game is the investment and grind. Even after only a couple of days it already takes SO MUCH WORK. That original career was 3 hours long since I was savoring it. Most of your grinding runs are going to be like 30-40 mins, and you have to do SO many of them in order to complete the events. You lose the ability to enjoy the emotional stakes and the stories and it’s just WORK. At least, I did. UPDATE: Auto Career (Independent Career) is a game changer! The game is playable now! Yay! Tl;dr: To put it simply: this has all the elements for a great casual or story game, but it’s still a little too grindy. Also, really don’t know why it’s even 12+. The fanservice is really mild. On a similar level as Bang Dream probably.

title: Made me learn something new.
body: I love this game for many reasons, like the storylines, the gambling aspect of course, but best of all.. its history. %95 of the characters from this game are inspired by real, Japanese race horses, that each have their own legacy that this game honors. I too began honoring the legacies these horses have had, such as Rice Shower and such. It also had made me learn more of a sport that I never thought I would love so much.. horse racing. From playing Umamusume: Pretty Derby for almost a year now, it's given me a big spark on horse racing, and has become one of my biggest interests. Any races my local race track has? I'll be watching them from TV, admiring everything there is to admire. I even went to my first horse race this year over at the Saratoga race track to witness the Belmont Stakes, where I got to see this year's Kentucky Derby winner Golden Tempo acquire the second leg of the triple crown and win. That was one of the best days I've had in a few months, and I'm planning again to go to the races to watch them in person. This game is the reason why I've discovered something new that's made me so happy, and I will continue to play this game continuously. I highly recommend this game to everyone who might like anime, horses, lore, or maybe all three of them at once.

title: unexpected favorite with surprisingly generous gacha
body: downloaded this game as a half joke after seeing it on youtube just to check it out maybe a month after release since i thought the fact that the characters are all based off real race horses was interesting. i wasn’t there from the beginning, but i’ve been playing close to a year now near daily so not far off. the game is surprisingly fun, the cross play between pc and ios is a great bonus to me personally. i’d describe the game as a gambling horse race take on deck building games and character collection gachas with a notable visual novel element too, which is great and free too. the gacha is generous in the game, but don’t misunderstand. its not generous because of the odds, but because of how generous the game is with the ability to earn premium currency while being f2p, as well as guarantees when doing x10 pulls. if you regularly play the game and complete events, it’s super possible to pull what you’re aiming for if you plan and save your currencies accordingly, and of course a bit of good luck. one of the few games i actually wouldn’t mind spending money on because it doesn’t feel predatory or forced and because i want to support this kind of f2p model for future games. an unexpected favorite game of mine to be honest
